messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — noticed a regression in tenant fairness after yesterday's batcher change. Short-sequence tenants are getting stalled behind long requests when KV hit-rate drops.
ahmed: Ugh, saw that too in canary. Tail latency for short sequences went from ~35ms P95 to ~220ms on some hosts.
chris: Any kernel selection shuffles tied to that deploy? I remember the change nudged some kernels to prefer long-prefetch paths.
sara: Yes, the runtime started favoring the 'prefetch-heavy' kernel when avg_seq_len > 128, but that decision is per-node and ignores queue composition.
maria: REPRO steps I used: ramp mixed traffic (30% short 8-32 token, 70% long 256-1024), disable KV warmup (~hit-rate drops 40%), watch short tenant queue depth. Shorts pile up even though they should be cheaper.
ev an: profiler-bot linked a flamegraph: https://profiler.internal/runs/1795001100 — shows cont_batcher stuck in large-window coalescer for ~70% of cycles.
profiler-bot: Snapshot metrics attached: kv_hit_rate=0.58, batch_window_ms=12.4, avg_tokens_per_batch=312, short_waits>50ms=820/min.
ahmed: Hypothesis: continuous batcher batches by token budget target without lane awareness; long sequences consume token budget, preventing short sequences from forming independent small batches.
chris: Suggestion: additive split — reserve a small token quota per short-lane that refills on every scheduling tick. Eg `short_quota_tokens = max(64, total_quota * 0.15)` so shorts can form micro-batches.
sara: Also consider KV bias: when KV hit-rate low, long requests do more compute and hog kernels. We can prefer kernel fastpath for short batches even if slightly suboptimal for long. That reduces tail.
maria: Quick config I'm proposing for an experiment:```json
{
  "batcher": {
    "token_target": 1024,
    "short_cutoff_tokens": 48,
    "short_reserved_frac": 0.18,
    "max_batch_window_ms": 8,
    "prefer_short_fastpath": true
  }
}
```
ahmed: We should also add a queue-age cap: evict/force-schedule any short request waiting >25ms into a dedicated micro-batch. Prevents starvation.
ev an: I'll wire telemetry: per-tenant short_wait_count, avg_short_wait_ms, kernel_switches, kv_hit_rate. Want to see P50/P95/P99 by tenant and seq-length buckets.
chris: Can we avoid extra descheduling churn? Maybe make the short quota refill smoothly (leaky-bucket) instead of hard reservation to keep throughput.
sara: Good call. Also plan a canary with 10% traffic and two modes: (A) prefer_short_fastpath on, (B) off. Compare unit-cost and tail-latency.
maria: Timeline: ahmed to patch batcher policy + add short quota leaky refill (today), evan to hook telemetry (today), canary tomorrow morning, collect 1h traces, meet 11am for results.
ahmed: Patch almost ready, pushing PR in ~30m: link https://git.internal/r/1795/queue-tilt.
ev an: Telemetry dashboards created: /dashboards/queue-tilt-adaptive. Will post first graphs once canary starts.
chris: One more safety: if prefer_short_fastpath increases model steps for long requests too much, fallback to current kernel after 5% throughput degradation window.
maria: Agreed — add auto-fallback threshold. Thanks team :thumbsup:
